metadata.source: Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972 - Glossary of Legal and Technical Terms

absolute_protection.definition: Highest level of legal protection where hunting, trade, and possession are completely prohibited except under extremely limited exceptions (e.g., Section 11 for human safety). Applies to Schedule I species.

appendix_i_ii_iii.definition: CITES (Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species) categorizes species by trade threat level. Appendix I: trade prohibited (except non-commercial). Appendix II: trade regulated with permits. Appendix III: species listed by individual countries for cooperation. Incorporated as Schedule IV in WLPA 2022.

captive_animal.definition: Any animal specified in Schedules I, II, III, or IV that is captured, kept, or bred in captivity. Requires ownership certificate (Section 42) and declaration (Section 40).

cites.definition: Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora (1973). International agreement regulating cross-border trade in wildlife. Implemented in India via WLPA Chapter VB (2022 Amendment).

community_reserve.definition: Protected area declared on private/community land where the community/landowner agrees to protect wildlife (Section 36C). Managed by a committee including the land owner, Forest Dept representative, and Panchayat/tribal representative. Introduced in 2002 Amendment.

conservation_reserve.definition: Protected area declared on government-owned land after consulting local communities (Section 36A). Managed by Conservation Reserve Management Committee. 2022 Amendment: Central Government can also declare. Less restrictive than sanctuary.

core_area.definition: Inviolate zone within a tiger reserve identified on scientific criteria as essential for tiger conservation (Section 38V Explanation I). No human activity permitted. Rights of Scheduled Tribes/forest dwellers protected. Buffer area surrounds it.

buffer_area.definition: Area surrounding the core zone in a tiger reserve where a degree of habitat protection ensures core integrity while promoting human-wildlife coexistence with recognition of livelihood rights (Section 38V Explanation II).

ecological_security.definition: Long title of WLPA since 2002 Amendment: 'ensuring the ecological and environmental security of the country'. Shifts focus from mere species protection to ecosystem-level security.

ex_gratia.definition: Discretionary compensation paid by State Government for crop damage, livestock loss, human injury/death due to wildlife. Not a legal right under WLPA but provided under State schemes. Section 60B allows rewards up to ₹10,000 for assistance in detection.

forfeiture.definition: Civil proceeding (Chapter VIA, Sections 58A-58Y) where property acquired from illegal hunting/trade is forfeited to State Government. Burden of proof on accused. Competent Authority, Appellate Tribunal, Administrator manage process.

government_property.definition: Section 39: All wild animals (Schedules I-IV), animal articles, trophies, meat, ivory, specified plants, and scheduled specimens (2022) are Government property. Live animals to be housed in recognized zoo/rescue centre. No commercial sale on disposal.

habitat.definition: The natural environment where a species lives, including all ecological factors. WLPA protects habitat through protected areas, sanctuary/NP restrictions (Sections 29, 35), and tiger reserve core-buffer model.

hunting.definition: Section 2(16): Killing, poisoning, capturing, coursing, snaring, trapping, driving, baiting any wild/captive animal AND every attempt to do so. Extremely broad - includes egg collection, nest disturbance, photography with disturbance.

invasive_alien_species.definition: Section 2(16A) (2022): Non-native animal/plant species whose introduction/spread threatens Indian wildlife/habitat. Central Govt can regulate/prohibit import, trade, possession, proliferation (Section 62A). Seizure and destruction authorized.

management_authority.definition: Section 49E (2022): Central Govt officer not below Additional DG Forests. Issues CITES permits/certificates (import/export/re-export/introduction from sea), submits reports, implements Convention. Designated ports only.

national_board.definition: Section 5A (2002): Apex advisory body chaired by Prime Minister. Vice-Chair: Environment Minister. 30+ members including MPs, NGOs, experts, Secretaries, Directors, CWLWs. Functions: policy, advice, protected areas, impact assessment, status reports.

ntca.definition: Chapter IVB (2006): Statutory body for tiger conservation. Chair: Environment Minister. Powers: approve Tiger Conservation Plans, disallow unsustainable land use in tiger reserves, tourism norms, human-wildlife conflict mitigation, direct States. Member-Secretary: IG Forests.

ownership_certificate.definition: Section 42: Legal document issued by CWLW proving lawful possession of captive animal/animal article/trophy. Required for transfer/transport (Section 43). 2022: Voluntary surrender cancels certificate (Section 42A), no compensation.

protected_area.definition: Section 2(24A) (2002): National Park, Sanctuary, Conservation Reserve, or Community Reserve notified under Sections 18, 35, 36A, 36C. Four-tier hierarchy of protection.

schedule.definition: Lists appended to WLPA categorizing species by protection level. 2022 restructure: Schedule I & II (animals - absolute/high protection), Schedule III (animals - moderate), Schedule IV (CITES species), Schedule V (vermin), Schedule VI (plants). Section 2(26A) defines 'Schedule'.

scientific_authority.definition: Section 49F (2022): Research institute(s) designated by Central Govt. Advises Management Authority on non-detriment findings (trade won't harm species survival), monitors Appendix II exports, limits export permits if needed.

scheduled_animal.definition: Section 49A/2(34A): Animal specified in Schedule I or Schedule II. Highest trade prohibition under Chapter VA (Sections 49A-49C). Trade completely banned after 'specified date' (2 months from listing).

scheduled_specimen.definition: Section 49D(k) (2022): Specimen of species listed in CITES Appendices I, II, III incorporated in Schedule IV. Includes whole animals/plants, readily recognizable parts/derivatives. CITES permits required for trade.

specified_plant.definition: Plant species listed in Schedule VI. Protected under Chapter IIIA (Sections 17A-17H). Picking, uprooting, collection, possession, trade prohibited. Cultivation/dealing requires licence. Becomes Government property (Section 17H).

tiger_reserve.definition: Area notified under Section 38V for tiger conservation. Comprises Core (critical tiger habitat - inviolate) and Buffer (coexistence zone). Requires NTCA-approved Tiger Conservation Plan. Voluntary relocation with consent/rehabilitation. No boundary change/de-notification without NTCA+National Board approval.

vermin.definition: Section 2(34): Wild animal notified by Central Govt under Section 62. 2022: ONLY Schedule II species eligible. Declared vermin loses Schedule II protection for notified area/period. No penalty for killing during notification.

voluntary_surrender.definition: Section 42A (2022): Person with ownership certificate can give 7 days notice and surrender captive animal/ivory to CWLW. Certificate cancelled. NO compensation. Surrendered items become State Govt property. Encourages compliance.

wccb.definition: Chapter IVC (2006, renamed 2022): Centralized wildlife crime intelligence agency. Director: Director of Wildlife Preservation. Officers from Police, Customs, Forest. Functions: intelligence, coordination, CITES implementation, international cooperation, capacity building, policy advice. Officers can file complaints (Section 55).
